svg.title: Circuits & components
svg.desc: Charge carries energy: Q = It; E = QV. C = A × s; V = J/C. Conventional current: + to − outside supply. Metal electrons move oppositely. A cell provides pd; it does not create charge. Resistance: R = V/I in Ω. At fixed V, greater R gives smaller I. Ammeter in series, voltmeter across component. Use standard symbols; a dot marks a junction. One loop: series: Same current throughout. Supply pd = sum of component pds. 4 Ω + 8 Ω across 12 V → 12 Ω total, 1 A; voltage drops 4 V and 8 V. Branches: parallel: Same pd across supply-connected branches; total I = sum of branch currents. Extra paths reduce total R. One broken branch need not stop others. Appliances can switch independently. Resistor & lamp: I vertical, V horizontal: ohmic line through origin at constant temperature; slope = 1/R. Lamp heats as current rises → ions vibrate more → R increases; curve flattens. Use V/I at a point. Diode & sensors: Diode: high reverse R; conducts forward with sufficient pd. LED emits light. Thermistor R decreases with temperature; thermostat. LDR R decreases with light; dark-triggered lamp controls.

g.text: Parallel paths share the same pd
